name: Young Marble Giants
label: Rough Trade
lede: Two brothers and a singer from Cardiff made one album with a drum machine played off a cassette, toured America, and split. Kurt Cobain, Courtney Love and Belle and Sebastian spent the next decades covering it.

eras.title: Cardiff, out of work, turned down low
eras.text: Punk was loud, so the Moxham brothers and Alison Statton went the other way: thin guitar, melodic bass, a near-whisper and a home-made rhythm box. Stuart Moxham told the Quietus they were all unemployed in Cardiff, which left plenty of time to work it out.

years.src: Pennyblackmusic · Far Out · Wikipedia: Young Marble Giants
years.h: Stuart Moxham leaves True Wheel and starts something quieter
years.p: Stuart sang in True Wheel, a Cardiff covers band named after a Brian Eno song, with his brother Philip on bass. He brought in Philip and [[Alison Statton|d03b561e-c65a-49bb-8edd-926433112e6b]], who were already working together, and cousin Peter Joyce.
years.xp:
Joyce was a telephone engineer who built his own synthesizer from a kit, and the band ran on tapes of his home-made drum machine because nobody wanted a drummer. They rehearsed in an old shop in Adamsdown, and Moxham soaked up dub from the Casablanca club and the Tiger Bay docks.

The name comes from the kouroi, the early Greek marble statues of young men. Moxham told Pennyblackmusic that Phil and Alison were "a musical unit" before he asked them in.

years.h: Wendy Smith lends Stuart the money for a Rickenbacker
years.p: Smith, Moxham's girlfriend and a Cardiff art student, paid for the Rickenbacker 425 that carries the band's sound. She also shot the early photos of the four-piece and later photographed the US tour.

years.h: Two songs on a Cardiff compilation land a Rough Trade album
years.p: The band's first vinyl is on Is the War Over?, an LP from the Cardiff DIY label Z Block. Rough Trade hears the two tracks and offers an album.

years.h: Five days at Foel Studios, drums played off a cassette
years.p: The record is cut near Welshpool with the studio's owner, ex-Hawkwind and Amon Düül II man Dave Anderson. The beats come from a cassette player and each song is mixed in about 20 minutes.
years.xp:
Many tracks are first takes. The only overdubs on the whole album are a slide guitar on Include Me Out and distorted vocals on Eating Noddemix.

Statton told Far Out nobody ever planned to flesh the songs out: "we were looking for a sound that was spacious."

eras.title: One album, one tour, one exit
eras.text: Colossal Youth became one of Rough Trade's big sellers and took the band to Berlin, Vancouver, Los Angeles and New York. Within about a year of its release the band was gone.

years.p: Rough Trade puts it out in February 1980 and it reaches No. 3 on the UK indie chart. The sleeve nods to the Beatles' With the Beatles.

years.h: Final Day goes to No. 6 and outlives the band
years.p: The single climbs the UK indie chart. [[Belle and Sebastian|e5c7b94f-e264-473c-bb0f-37c85d4d5c70]] and [[Galaxie 500|4de3cfed-b459-42bd-bfbb-7a843fbc73df]] later covered Final Day, and the Pitchfork 500 includes the original.

yt: Choci Loni, live at Futurama 2, Leeds, September 1980
years.h: A drum machine at a goth festival: Futurama 2 in Leeds
years.p: The band plays the Futurama festival at Leeds' Queens Hall. Live tapes from the weekend survive, including Choci Loni.

yt: Live at the Western Front, Vancouver, November 6, 1980
years.h: Vancouver's Western Front gets the whole hush
years.p: The North American tour, with [[Cabaret Voltaire|439a29ad-f4ef-4857-a7cd-3d4a551056c8]] among the touring company, stops at the Western Front arts space in Vancouver. The set was filmed.

years.cap: Young Marble Giants live as a trio, c. 1980
years.src: New York Times · Wikipedia: Young Marble Giants
yt: Final Day, live at Hurrah, New York, 1980
years.h: The New York Times shows up for the Hoboken debut and the gear fails
years.p: John Rockwell had called Colossal Youth one of the most striking records of recent months. At Maxwell's in Hoboken the equipment acted up and the balances were off; Hurrah in Manhattan came the next Friday.
years.xp: Rockwell still liked the sound: two tall brothers, a small singer and a rhythm box he compared to Suicide's. A recording from the Hurrah stand later came out as Live at the Hurrah! (2004).

years.h: The Testcard EP is their highest indie chart placing
years.p: Rough Trade releases Testcard in March 1981 and it reaches No. 2 on the UK indie chart, one place higher than the album.

years.big: "Tired and emotional bollocks, ego, and so on."
q: Treat it as a professional occupation rather than a vehicle for my hangups.
years.h: Young Marble Giants split after the American tour
years.p: That's Stuart Moxham in 2002, on reasons he says were never discussed. He told the Quietus the American tour was too big to handle.
years.xp:
Alex Ogg's Quietus interview adds that Phil and Alison's relationship was coming apart at the same time. Moxham told Pennyblackmusic he spent years thinking about a reunion that the others didn't want, and that a Rough Trade anniversary gig was the closest they came.

What he'd do differently: not let it dissolve.

years.cap: Alison Statton and Simon Booth with Weekend, Paradiso, Amsterdam
years.h: The Gist, Weekend and a Communards bassist
years.p: Stuart forms The Gist, whose Love at First Sight becomes a European hit for Étienne Daho as Paris, Le Flore. Statton starts the jazz-leaning Weekend with Phil on bass.
years.xp:
Stuart also made Embrace the Herd (1982) for Rough Trade, mostly at home after a bad motorbike accident. Phil went on to play bass for The Communards and [[Everything but the Girl|959cf5bf-ee29-4af6-a85a-0b480181d988]], touring Love Not Money with them in 1985, and worked with [[David Thomas|b6459915-9b42-477a-aa17-fdcae9ff2d13]] and the Pedestrians.

By 2002, Moxham said, Statton was a chiropractor in Cardiff and Phil was looking after polo ponies.

eras.title: Kurt Cobain's record collection, then a barn in Hay
eras.text: Cobain's lists turned a Cardiff one-off into a reference point for American indie. The trio came back for a one-off in 2007 and kept saying yes for eight more years.

yt: KEXP Cobain 50: Stuart Moxham on Colossal Youth
years.h: Kurt Cobain names Colossal Youth among his ten key records
years.p: In Melody Maker, Cobain calls it total atmospherics. [[Hole|1dcc8968-f2cd-441c-beda-6270f70f2863]] put Credit in the Straight World on Live Through This in 1994.
years.xp:
Cobain also wrote it into his top-50 albums list and had planned to cover the same song himself. Stephin Merritt said the album was the main template for [[The Magnetic Fields|3ff72a59-f39d-411d-9f93-2d4a86413013]]' debut, and covered The Man Amplifier.

In 2025 Stuart Moxham talked through the album on KEXP's Cobain 50 podcast.

years.h: BBC Radio Wales gets the trio back, and one new song
years.p: Statton and the Moxham brothers reunite for a Radio Wales special and play a new song, Alright.

years.cap: Young Marble Giants at Clyro Court, near Hay-on-Wye, May 2007
years.src: The Guardian · Wikipedia: Colossal Youth · Wikipedia: Young Marble Giants
years.h: First gig in 27 years, in the barn of a country hotel
years.p: A couple of hundred rain-soaked fans file into Clyro Court for the Hay-on-Wye Festival show. Moxham reads from notes and jokes about a difficult second album.
years.xp:
The show marked Domino's reissue, Colossal Youth & Collected Works, out July 9, 2007 with the EPs, the single and the Is the War Over? tracks. The Guardian's Tom Hughes called the performance faultless and said it didn't feel like a cash-in.

It was billed as a one-off. In October they played the BB Mix festival outside Paris with younger brother Andrew Moxham on electronic drums in place of the old machine.

years.h: Primavera Sound books the Cardiff trio
years.p: Barcelona's festival puts the reunited band on its 2008 bill, with Andrew Moxham now on drums. Berlin's Hebbel am Ufer theatre follows in January 2009.

years.cap: Young Marble Giants playing Colossal Youth at All Tomorrow's Parties, Minehead, May 2009
years.h: Colossal Youth start to finish at All Tomorrow's Parties
years.p: The band plays the whole album at ATP in Minehead. [[Jeff Mangum|6a7b9d5e-a863-4a90-a056-77942e9f43de]] of [[Neutral Milk Hotel|a506f761-2c22-4b2f-8a94-bd748c2c8f75]] brings them back to Minehead for the ATP he curated in March 2012.

years.h: Stuart Moxham posts that the band is no more
years.p: The announcement goes up on the band's Facebook page. The last documented dates were Manchester and Glasgow in October 2014 and Marseille's MIMI festival in July 2015.
